answer: The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the vertex funding graph is rebuilt from the delta history every epoch. Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 264 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator forfeits 264 bonds yet holds one position, and the karst report publishes the merged exposure. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
